note: What a server streaming a match sends to carry one fragment of a chunk or key frame of recorded messages (see spec/spectating.md). A client takes a chunk's facts from its fragment 0, appends fragments in arrival order, and holds the chunk complete at the fragment whose index is one less than the count. A new fragment 0 drops a chunk left unfinished, and a fragment with no chunk begun is dropped. The header carries zero.

fields.name: chunk
fields.note: The chunk's id, or the key frame's. Chunk 0 is dropped; chunks play in order from 1, and a missing one stalls the stream. Key frames count separately, from 1.

fields.name: fragments
fields.note: How many fragments the chunk is cut into.

3.name: endOfStartup
3.note: The last chunk of the match's setting up.

4.name: gameStart
4.note: The chunk the match proper begins with.

5.name: startup
5.note: A chunk of the match's setting up.

fields.name: size
fields.note: The whole chunk's size in bytes. A client does not check fragments against it, so they must not exceed it.

fields.name: duration
fields.note: Seconds the chunk covers; it only shapes the estimate of when the last chunk ends.

fields.name: nextChunk
fields.note: For a key frame, the ordinary chunk to go on from. Where zero, a client takes key frame interval over chunk interval, times the key frame's id less one, plus the start-game chunk.

fields.name: data
fields.note: This fragment's bytes of the chunk, to the end of the message.
